Construct a validated instrument of items

instrument.Rd

Bundles the questions to be answered, the labels the model may answer with, and the instruction that elicits them.

Usage

instrument(
  items,
  labels = c("YES", "NO"),
  ...,
  definitions = NULL,
  scores = NULL,
  exclusive = FALSE,
  exact = FALSE,
  probe_texts = NULL,
  cue = NULL,
  lang = c("en", "es"),
  medium = NULL,
  text_label = NULL,
  answer_label = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  backend = NULL
)

Arguments

items

A named list or named character vector of question strings. An unnamed single string is accepted and named Q1. When exclusive = TRUE, this may instead be a stem name ("primary" or "best") or a custom question, with the categories supplied through labels.

A question is a free string and it is yours. It may run to a paragraph, reproduce a codebook definition verbatim, carry an exclusion clause, or include worked examples. Nothing about the scoring changes, since the question sits in the prompt and the answer is read from one token.

labels

A character vector of answer words, at least two. Each element is its own label. Matching is case folded and reads by prefix, so a token counts when it opens a label and a tokenizer splitting PRESUPUESTO into P still scores. Text explaining what a label means goes in definitions, not here.

One word each, and whitespace is refused. NOT_SURE and NOT-SURE build, since joining leaves a single answer word that a tokenizer may split into a prefix of itself. NOT SURE does not, since one token cannot span the space and the label would be matched by NOT alone. Default is c("YES", "NO").

...

Not used, and refused if anything reaches it. Every argument after it is name-only, so a misspelling lands here rather than being matched by position.

definitions

A named character vector explaining what each label means, or NULL (the default). An exclusive instrument lists these in the question, so the model reads the explanation and types only the name. Any instrument can carry them, where they appear in print() and improve the generated probe document.

scores

A named numeric vector giving each label a value, or NULL (the default). Names must match the label names exactly. Supplying them asserts that the spacing between the numbers is meaningful, which is what makes an average of them defined and is a stronger claim than that the labels are ordered. Nothing checks it, since unequal spacing is legitimate on a real scale.

exclusive

A logical value indicating whether to build an exclusive-choice instrument. One question lists all K categories, the model picks one, and all K share a softmax at position 1. The result is a distribution, unlike an instrument of independent binary items. The category names become answer tokens here, so they must differ at their first character. Default is FALSE.

exact

A logical value indicating whether to score by exact match against discovered tokens rather than by prefix. Requires backend, since those tokens come from probing.

This is the one case where a label carries more than one string. Prefix matching needs the labels to differ at their first character, because a split label often emits only that character and E cannot be attributed between economia and educacion. Probing sends one throwaway document per label, reads back what the model actually writes, ECON and EDUC, and records it. Scoring then consults that record instead of guessing from a prefix, and a bare E counts for nothing and shows up in prob_other rather than being assigned to whichever label sorted first.

Nobody types those entries. Use exact when the labels cannot be made to differ at their first character, and rename them if they can. Default is FALSE.

probe_texts

A named character vector of example documents, one per label, used in place of the generated probe document, or NULL (the default). Supply these when the labels describe a property of the text rather than a topic, since the generated document is about the label rather than one that exhibits it.

cue

A string giving the instruction appended after each question. Generated from labels and lang if NULL. Supply your own for a language without a preset.

lang

A string giving the language preset for the prompt scaffolding, "en" (the default) or "es". Sets cue, text_label, and answer_label together, and any of the three can still be overridden individually. For any other language, pass all three explicitly rather than expecting a preset. See the section below for what each preset contains.

This is the scaffolding, not the question. A question written in Spanish under the default "en" preset produces a Spanish item wrapped in an English cue, which is a real prompt and rarely the intended one.

medium

A string naming the stem set a preset name is looked up in, one of "text", "audio", "image" or "video". Read only when items names a preset, since a literal question carries its own wording. There is no default, because the sets are not translations of one another. A picture mentions nothing, so image has show and depict where text has topic and mention, and video has both plus discuss, since a row holds frames and a transcript at once and the verb is what says which one the question is about.

text_label, answer_label

Strings giving the prompt scaffolding. Default to the lang preset.

name

A string giving a label for the instrument, carried into provenance, or NULL (the default).

backend

An ollama_backend() object, or NULL (the default). When supplied, each label is probed against a production-shaped prompt and its observed first token is recorded. Probing checks that the labels are distinguishable at position 1 and prints what each one emits. It changes scoring only under exact = TRUE, since a discovered token already opens its own label and so is matched by prefix regardless.

Value

An object of class fathom_instrument, a list. Its print method shows the parts usually wanted, and preview() shows what the model will receive, before Ollama applies the model's chat template.

The instrument

  • items is the named list of questions, one per item, in the order declared. That order is the order item_report() and the results use, so an instrument reads as the questionnaire it was written as.

  • labels is the named list of answer labels.

  • normalized holds what each label is actually matched against. Under prefix matching this is the label itself, and under exact = TRUE it is the variants probing discovered. This is the field to read to find out why a token did or did not count.

  • definitions is the category text shown to the model beneath the question, or NULL. Where long category wording goes, since it has no first-character constraint on it.

  • scores is the numeric value per label, or NULL. Sits outside the prompt hash on purpose, so rescaling re-extracts nothing.

How it gets asked

  • cue is the assembled instruction naming the permitted answers.

  • text_label and answer_label are the words introducing the document and the answer slot.

  • lang names which scaffolding preset supplied the three above.

Shape and mode

  • exclusive says whether the labels share one distribution. FALSE gives independent binary items, so a document may match several.

  • exact_match says whether scoring compares against probed tokens rather than by prefix. The escape for a label set that has to collide.

  • k and n_items are the counts of labels and of items.

  • name is the short label-set name used in printing.

Implementation

probe_texts and firsts are implementation. They hold what probing was run against and the token each label emitted when probed, and neither is a stable interface.

Label matching

Scoring reads one token and counts it as a label when it opens that label, so BU counts as BUDGET. Nothing has to be discovered first, because a model writing BUDGET must emit a prefix of it, and that follows from every tokenizer in use detokenizing by concatenation rather than from any one model's vocabulary.

The price is that labels must differ at their first character. Under prefix matching this is checked at construction from the strings alone, with no backend. A split label frequently emits only its first character, and two labels sharing one cannot then be told apart. With distinct first characters no two labels share any prefix, so every match resolves to one label.

A label carrying whitespace is refused at construction, because scoring reads one token. One token cannot span a space, so a two-word label is matched by its opening word and the rest is never read, which scores the opening word rather than scoring zero. Join the words if the answer really is compound, since NOT_SURE and NOT-SURE are both accepted.

exact = TRUE is the way out when they have to collide. Each label is probed once, the emitted token is recorded, and scoring consults that record instead of reading a prefix. Passing a backend alone runs the probe without changing how scoring works, which is worth doing once on a new model to see the token map.

Labels and definitions

Labels and definitions are different things. labels names the answer words and the surface forms they may appear in. definitions holds the text a reader or a model needs to know what a label means. Keeping them apart matters because scoring matches the token at position 1 against labels, so a definition sitting in labels registers a token the model never emits and that label scores zero on every document with no error raised.

An exclusive instrument lists the definitions under its question, which is what lets a category be a long phrase while the answer stays one word. Other instruments store them without putting them in the prompt, since their question is yours to write.

Items or one exclusive question

An instrument of items asks about each category on its own, so a document can carry several categories or none, and each question is answered without the others in view. exclusive = TRUE asks one question that lists every category, so the categories share one distribution and each document takes one of them.

The exclusive form is the one to use when a document should take exactly one category, such as a level on a scale, and whenever the categories are defined against each other. Halterman and Keith (2026) found no accuracy gain in preliminary experiments from asking about one category at a time, and argue that their codebooks need every category in view to separate them. A drone strike can meet a codebook's definition of an assassination for a model that never sees the drone assassination category beside it.

Twenty alternatives

Ollama returns at most the 20 most likely first tokens. A label the model does not rank among those 20 on a document scores exactly 0 there, and on two labels its partner then scores exactly 1. Every label therefore has to be a word the model would plausibly open its answer with, likely enough to rank among the 20. An instrument of many labels risks some of them falling outside on every document. pct_label_absent in item_report() reports the share of calls where any label did.

Ordinal labels

scores attaches a numeric value to each label. The values are metadata. They never appear in the prompt and the model never types them, so the labels stay semantic words.

Scoring then returns an expected_score column, the sum of each label's value weighted by its renormalized probability. The labels of any one call share a softmax, since they are read at a single position from a single distribution, so this works on any instrument rather than only exclusive ones.

Nothing checks that the labels are ordered. scores asserts an order the package cannot verify, and reversing the values reverses every score without complaint.

Language presets

Three strings the prompt is built from, plus the word used to join the labels inside the cue.

partenes
text_labelTextTexto
answer_labelAnswerRespuesta
label joineroro
cueAnswer with exactly one word: ...Responde con exactamente una palabra: ...

So a two-label instrument under lang = "es" closes with Responde con exactamente una palabra: sí o no. and labels its parts Texto and Respuesta.

Two stems ship for exclusive = TRUE, in both languages, and unlike the item stems in template_items() neither takes a {label}, since the categories arrive through definitions instead.

stemenes
"primary"What is the PRIMARY subject of this text?¿Cuál es el tema PRINCIPAL de este texto?
"best"Which category best describes this text?¿Qué categoría describe mejor este texto?

They are not interchangeable. "primary" asks what the text is about, which assumes the categories are subjects. "best" asks which category describes it, which assumes only that they are a scheme worth sorting into. Any other string is used as the question verbatim, in whatever language it is written.

Case folding and accented labels

A generated token is folded to upper case before it is compared to a label, so sí, Sí, and SÍ all count as one answer.

preview() and check_backend() fold the same way, which is what makes the preview table a reliable picture of what scoring will do.

The first-character rule is therefore about characters and not bytes. Two labels differing only in an accent still collide once folded, and this function refuses them. Where a coding scheme forces that collision, exact = TRUE is the escape.

References

Halterman, A. and Keith, K. A. (2026). Codebook LLMs. Evaluating LLMs as measurement tools for political science concepts. Political Analysis 34, 188–204. doi:10.1017/pan.2025.10017

See also

template_items() for items built from one stem, preview() for the prompt it assembles, and measure() for running it.

Examples

b <- instrument(
  items = list(
    econ = "Does the text discuss economic conditions?",
    immig = "Does the text discuss immigration?"
  ),
  labels = c("YES", "NO")
)
b
#> Instrument
#> 
#> Shape         independent items
#> Items         2 (econ, immig)
#> Labels        2 (YES, NO)
#> Cue           \n\nAnswer with exactly one word: YES or NO.
#> Matching      by prefix, so a token counts when it opens a label
